correctness.rationale: Each active delay is the Fourier transform of a row of exact overlap support. Full column rank of a reduced Fourier submatrix certifies full rank in characteristic zero by the nonvanishing minor. Independently, fraction-free elimination in Z[ζ₆] verified the four families directly among all 3969 nonempty support pairs: 50 at lower bound 6, all others at least 12. Singletons give six. Opposite two-point rows have Fourier support 3 or 6 and there are two active rows. Three-point cosets have three active rows with even supports: a hypothetical total 8 gives two single-character rows on the subgroup, whose quotient forces successive translated window ratios to be scalar characters and forces the third row also to be a single character. For two full supports, total 7 or 8 would leave at least four single-character rows; two have adjacent delays and their quotient forces the scalar character property at every delay. Finally the exact witness has profiles 1+4(−1)^ℓ and 2+2(−1)^ℓ in delays 0 and 3, respectively, with other delays zero. A delta pair attains six.
residual_risks: The rank computation establishes lower bounds, not realization of any row support. Attainment is separately symbolic; the conclusion is only about the first gap and not the rest of the spectrum.

value.rationale: This determines the first departure from the universal minimum in the smallest cyclic group with two distinct nontrivial proper subgroup orders, where prime-order arguments do not apply. The exclusion holds uniformly for both inputs, and an exact realizing witness makes the gap sharp rather than merely a lower bound from a finite sample.
residual_risks: No claim of a new general uncertainty principle, complete support spectrum, or classification of all extremizing pairs.
